body.statement:
At the selected-law factorization level, \(\mathfrak M\) is the finite four-response-type specialization of Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026). The design-A fiber \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) is the subfiber obtained by fixing the target-population cell margins \(P(E)=m\). The design-B fiber \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) satisfies their equation (13), together with instrument relevance. Consequently, on every compatible design-A law satisfying their regular Conditions 2--3, Theorem 1 transfers by restriction and the value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals their PN/PS value from Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). On every compatible regular design-B law satisfying Conditions 2--3, Corollary 1 transfers directly and \(\mathscr A\) returns the same PN/PS value.

The additional contribution is classification on compatible singular and boundary observable laws, including design-A rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, and forced-zero incident coefficients and the analogous design-B response-level shared-\(Z\) residual-forest strata. On every such compatible law the atlas returns either an exact target-rigidity certificate or legal target-changing full-SCM twins; an empty fiber is reported separately as incompatibility. This is a strict compatible singular/boundary classification extension, not an extension of the published regular formula and not a blanket subsumption claim.
body.justification: The theorem states the exact published transfer: Theorem 1 by fixed-margin restriction in design A and Corollary 1 through equation (13) in design B.
body.gap: The published regular formulas do not classify compatible singular and boundary fibers or incompatible inputs.
body.consumer: Users can separate regular formula agreement from the new singular-boundary classification without a subsumption claim.
body.proof_tex:
Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki has the selected-law factorization
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)
 =p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
   p(w\mid u)p(z\mid u)p(u). \tag{19}
\]
In the present model, response consistency makes \(p(y\mid x,u)\) the
deterministic kernel encoded by the four response types.  Outcome-dependent
selection supplies \(p(s\mid x,y)\), proxy exclusion supplies
\(p(w\mid u)\), and the definitions of the treatment, second-proxy, and
response-type mechanisms supply the remaining factors.  Thus, at this
factorization level, \(\mathfrak M\) is precisely the finite four-response-type
specialization of Condition 1.

The design-A definition adds
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,
 \qquad P_{\vartheta}(E)=m. \tag{20}
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) is the subfiber obtained by fixing the
population cell margins.  On a compatible member satisfying the published
regular Conditions 2--3, the cited regular-identification lemma applies
pointwise.  If \(R_A(p)\) denotes the pair computed by Appendix equations
(A.28)--(A.33), it gives
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_A(p)
 \quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m). \tag{21}
\]
Compatibility makes this fiber nonempty, so
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{R_A(p)\}. \tag{22}
\]
The full-rigidity theorem returns the unique element of this target set;
hence the returned value is the published one.  This is transfer by
restriction: fixing \(m\) does not weaken a conclusion already valid for
every member of the larger regular fiber.

For design B, instrument exogeneity changes the final two factors of (19) to
\(p(z\mid u)p(u)=g(z)p(u)\).  Hence every member obeys
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)
 =p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
   p(w\mid u)g(z)p(u), \tag{23}
\]
which is equation (13) of the cited paper.  The definition of
\(\mathcal F_B(p)\) additionally imposes the displayed instrument-relevance
inequality.  On a compatible law satisfying Conditions 2--3, the cited
regular IV identification result applies directly to (23).  Writing its
observable answer as \(R_B(p)\),
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_B(p)
 \quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p),
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_B(p)=\{R_B(p)\}. \tag{24}
\]
The full-rigidity theorem again forces the compiler to return this unique
value.

Neither (21) nor (24) is invoked outside the published regular conditions.
There the mixed-support theorem exhausts rank-two orientations, rank-one
\(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes, all coefficient-support
faces, shared endpoints, and, in design B, all residual-forest and active-cycle
states.  The full-rigidity theorem consequently returns either the common
exact target or legal target-changing SCM lifts on every compatible singular
or boundary law, while (15)--(16) of its proof distinguish incompatibility.
This proves a compatible singular/boundary classification extension only; it
neither enlarges the domain of the published regular formula nor asserts
blanket subsumption.
